sources.entry: UTM - UTM is an easy-to-use GUI for QEMU and can run ARM64, x64 and other VMs on M1 Macs. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/utmapp/UTM)

summary.name: UTM
summary.one_liner: UTM is a free, open-source macOS app for running Windows, Linux, macOS and classic operating systems in virtual machines or emulation, built on QEMU and Apple's Virtualization framework.
keywords: run games on mac virtual machine
use_cases: Run Windows or Linux on an Apple Silicon Mac
Emulate older PowerPC, SPARC or x86 operating systems
Run multiple macOS instances for development
Automate virtual machines with AppleScript or utmctl
Run DOS or lightweight Linux on iOS with UTM SE
summary.what_it_does: UTM runs ARM64 operating systems on Apple Silicon using Apple's Hypervisor framework at near-native speed, and emulates Intel x86/x64 plus other architectures such as ARM32, MIPS, PPC and RISC-V more slowly. It is built on QEMU and can also use Apple Virtualization for macOS and Linux guests. VMs can be created, configured and controlled through AppleScript or the utmctl command line tool, which supports start, stop, suspend, snapshots and USB connections. The page also describes UTM SE for iOS, a slimmer emulation-only build, and UTM Remote for controlling the Mac app from an iPhone or iPad.
notable: Built on QEMU with a simpler GUI and Apple Virtualization support
Scriptable via AppleScript and utmctl CLI with snapshots and USB passthrough
UTM SE for iOS runs emulation-only for older systems like DOS
Free and open source; Mac App Store version has the same features
caveats: Running x86/x64 and other non-ARM64 systems on Apple Silicon uses slower emulation
Virtualizing macOS requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS Monterey or later
Game support is ongoing work and compatibility varies
